Mr. J Handique, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the Competent Authority of Land Acquisition (CALA) and Mr. C Baruah, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the NHAI.
2. This Court has also heard Mr. P Mahanta, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.8.

sentences.text: During the course of the hearing, the learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner drew the attention of this Court to the orders dated 29.08.2024 and 23.09.2024, wherein it has been categorically admitted by the CALA that the petitioner was actually entitled to compensation for structural damages, but the amount was wrongly released to the respondent No.8.

Further to that,
during the course of the hearing, Mr. J Handique, the learned Government Advocate has also produced one document to the effect that steps for recovery of compensation amounting to Rs.50,21,953/- which was received by the respondent No.8 has been initiated.

It was also mentioned that while taking the steps, the respondent No.8 had initially agreed to refund the amount, but later on, had refused to do so and under such circumstances, the competent authority is proposing to initiate necessary steps to recover the amount under the Bengal Public Demands Recovery Act, 1913 .

In that regard, the communication which has been submitted before this Court is kept on record and marked with the letter 'X'.
4.

Mr. P Mahanta, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.8 submitted that the respondent No.8 rightly received the compensation amount taking into account that the respondent No.8 had an RCC building, which was also acquired for the four-laning of the National Highway 37.

He, Page No.# 4/4 further, submitted that all these aspects would be clear, inasmuch as, the respondent No.8 had also submitted his claim before the competent authority, prior to the determination of compensation in terms with Section 3G(1) of the National Highway Act, 1956.

5. Upon hearing the counsels, it appears that for deciding the dispute, the records pertaining to the determination of compensation by the competent authority, in so far as the lands, which are in dispute in the instant proceedings would be required to be looked into.
6. This Court, therefore, directs Mr. J Handique, the learned Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the CALA to produce those records on the next date.

7. This Court further puts a question upon both Mr. J Handique, the learned Government Advocate as well as Mr. C Baruah, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respective authorities as to whether the petitioner herein can be deprived of the amount to which the petitioner admittedly is entitled to as per law and whether further delay in disbursing the amount to the petitioner which the respondent authorities duly admit that the petitioner is entitled to would not lead to further accruing of interest thereby affecting the public exchequer.
8.
The learned counsels appearing on behalf of the CALA as well as NHAI authorities submitted that they would seek instruction(s) in that regard.

9. List the matter again on 11.02.2025 for further hearing.
